Priya (CS): FYI customer reported a quantized endpoint (4-bit/INT8 mix) is slower and lower-quality than the same model on FP16. they hit it in production ~1h ago. CC @Mateo (eng-runtime)
Mateo (eng-runtime): Ugh, thanks. do we have a concrete repro (input size, seq len, model variant, route) + p50/p95/throughput numbers?
Priya (CS): Repro from customer: endpoint: /v1/engines/rdw-text-7b-quantized, payload: typical chat history ~512 tokens + 128 generation. They see p50=220ms token vs fp16 p50=120ms token; overall latency 1.8x and higher perplexity on their eval set. Quick logs attached below (sanitized).
Priya (CS): ```
request: model=rdw-text-7b-quant, seq=640, gen=128, batch=1
metrics: tokens_per_sec=220, median_step_latency=120ms_per_token?? (customer-reported summary)
error: sometimes outputs shorter + odd tokenization artifacts
```
Mateo (eng-runtime): Thanks. can you paste the request headers (routing hints) and whether they used caching/kv_cache TTL? Also which runtime commit/hash are they on (hosted vs dedicated)?
Priya (CS): Hosted. runtime version: rwinf-2026.02.11-3f2b. routing: default (smart-routing enabled), kv_cache: enabled, cache_mode=global, batching: default autoscale. Customer says they didn't change client.
Mateo (eng-runtime): I started a quick local repro (same runtime hash). Early signal: when quant kernels are selected we sometimes fall back on slower reference kernels when calibration ranges mismatch => extra dtype casting + memcpy. Also observed increased KV cache misses because quantized variant uses a different key representation and we didn't normalize cache keys across variants. Profiling snippet: 
```
[profiling] kernel_select: int8_matmul -> fallback_ref_matmul (2.7x slower)
[profiling] memcopy: 12.3ms per step (dtype conversion)
[kv_cache] miss_rate: 37% (quant) vs 5% (fp16)
[batch] avg_batch_size_quant=1.2 vs fp16=4.8 (batching heuristics deprioritizing quant endpoints)
```
Mateo (eng-runtime): Root causes (likely): 1) calibration mismatch causing kernel selector to choose safe/reference path, 2) cache key divergence causing poor prefix reuse, 3) batching policy deprioritizes quantized variants (we schedule to cheaper buckets but end up with low batch sizes).
Alex (infra): For quick mitigation we can: a) route this customer to fp16 variant (fastest), b) force-int8-fast kernel override (unsafe but faster) via env RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=int8_fast on their pool, c) normalize kv cache key layer to include quantization tag so we can reuse prefix across variants (deploy-level). Which do we want to try first?
Jin (mlperf): Also calibration: their model was quantized with per-channel asymmetric calibration using a small sample. Increasing calibration samples and switching to symmetric (or using per-tensor quant) often fixes fallback. We should run a micro-benchmark: re-calibrate with 5k representative tokens and measure kernel selection trace.
Priya (CS): Customer wants a quick fix; they'll accept routing to FP16 for now if we can give ETA to restore quant perf. Can we do a canary route to FP16 immediately?
Mateo (eng-runtime): Yes — we can set a route override for that customer to rdw-text-7b-fp16 for 100% or do canary 10%. I recommend 100% until we stabilize quant variant. I'll also run a targeted profiler on the quant variant to confirm fallback.
SRE-bot: deploy: created route-override for customer_id=cust-327: rdw-text-7b-fp16 -> applied to 2 nodes (canary). timestamp=1760874520
Mateo (eng-runtime): Followups: 1) I'll add a unit in kernel selector to emit a histogram of fallback reasons (range overflow, NaN guard, unsupported layout). 2) We should normalize kv cache key encoding across quant/fp16 before wider rollout. 3) Short-term advice: disable long batching for quant endpoints (set MAX_BATCH_DELAY_MS=5) to avoid head-of-line small-batch penalties.
Alex (infra): I can spin a short patch to expose RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE for dedicated pools if we need it later.  ETA a few hours.
Jin (mlperf): I'll start a calibration run with 10k tokens and test kernel traces. If symmetric per-channel reduces fallbacks, we can publish a recommender in Optimize.
Priya (CS): I'll tell the customer we've routed them to FP16 canary and we're investigating root cause. ask them for an anonymized prompt set (50 samples) for our quality regression checks.
Customer-ops: Thanks — appreciate the fast action. Please keep us posted; we'll hold on any config changes.
Mateo (eng-runtime): Will follow up in-thread with profiler dumps and a short postmortem once we have evidence. short-term action items: route->fp16 (done), run calibration+kernel trace (in progress), kv cache key normalization spec (PR wip).
Priya (CS): Drafted customer message: "We've temporarily routed your traffic to FP16 to restore latency/quality. Our engineers are investigating quant kernel fallbacks and cache interactions; we'll share a timeline within 24h."  :thumbsup:
Mateo (eng-runtime): Nice. tagging this for eng-runtime postmortem. I'll attach flamegraph + kernel traces when ready.
SRE-bot: note: incident ticket #INF-2026-118 opened and linked to this thread.
